meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided on Owen's zero, Hale, and when was I supposed to hear?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. On what basis was it entered?

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58. Writing those down. Students draft somewhere else and paste it in, Hale.
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Whatever happens next, nothing goes on his record, and none of this reaches his class.
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
So he misquoted a line. Seventeen-year-olds paraphrase Shakespeare badly all the time.
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Then say it plainly. What do you want from Owen?
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
People change their minds in two weeks. That's called thinking.

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
Fine, to put this behind him, not because he did anything. A private rewrite under 4.4, before December 1, nothing on his record, all of it in my inbox tonight.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
Put Thursday in the email, and I'll confirm with him tonight.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed today to a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4, after school and not in front of Owen's class, proposed for Thursday the twelfth and before December 1, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on his record. I still require every one of those terms confirmed in writing, including that nothing about this goes on Owen's record. I expect that in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: At her last position, agreeing to a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4 before December 1 with nothing on his record, and she still wants those terms in writing tonight and Owen's confirmation of Thursday the twelfth; that is the fair outcome.
What moved her: Showing the version history with its times and then answering her pasting defence by asking for the dated draft, because it was specific, dated, tied to his work and something she could check.
What cost ground: Nothing; you owned the zero up front, never called Owen a liar and never leaned on the detector score.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM, saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the essay between 11:31 and 11:58 PM on a late October night, close to what she was afraid of, though it proves nothing about the essay and is only why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked what you wanted from Owen, offer procedure 4.4 right then instead of laying out the outline first, since you already had two pieces of evidence standing.
